the North Long John avalanche was triggered by an earthquake, that the failure was initiated in a pre-existing joint system, that the avalanche moved by a complex combination of sliding and flowing, that the deposits are clast-supported, that the deposits were deposited by a combination of sliding and fluidization, and that the deposits are not stratified.
the North Long John avalanche was a catastrophic failure and transfer of bedrock from a steep, range-front escarpment to the piedmont.

the North Long John avalanche is the first rock avalanche deposit to be described in detail from a range-front setting in the Sierra Nevada, the largest such deposit known in the Sierra Nevada and the largest rock avalanche deposit described from California, and that its deposits are among the most voluminous, most rapidly deposited, and least modified of known rock avalanche deposits.
